description: REQ-307's own canonical 9-step call order (contracts/sprint-2.md CRIT-201's binding authority; behavioral-spec.md's 'Canonical call order' under REQ-307) has NO step that records a real deploy's settled shelter cost to shelter-cost-ledger.js -- steps are: 1 home-check, 2 EVM keygen, 3 selectCloudTarget, 4 Solana keygen, 5 deploy, 6 ERC-8004 registration, 7 mcp.json write, 8 buildChildSpec, 9 ledger/registry append. Confirmed by direct source read: spawn-orchestrator.mjs's defaultDeploy (lines 230-257) returns {ok:true, leaseId, shelterCostUsd:null} -- shelterCostUsd is a HARDCODED null literal, never computed from a real settled cost -- and the calling site in executeSpawnAttempt (lines 453-465) never even assigns deployStep.value to a variable, so BOTH leaseId and shelterCostUsd are discarded immediately after the deploy step succeeds; shelter-cost-ledger.js::appendShelterCostEntry is never imported or called anywhere in spawn-orchestrator.mjs, run.sh, or wake-gate.mjs (confirmed by repo-wide grep; the only production reference to shelter-cost-ledger.js is wake-gate.mjs's read-only readShelterCostEntries import). Yet PROP-303c (verification-architecture.md line 490, Tier 1/2, required:true) explicitly specifies 'the real AKASH_DEPOSIT and settled lease cost are appended, via shelter-cost-ledger.js::appendShelterCostEntry, to the shelter-cost ledger' -- and sprint-1's own Phase 5 marked it 'proved' (verification/verification-report.md:128, verification/fuzz-results/full-suite-116-run.log & full-suite-121-run.log both show 'PASS PROP-303c'). That proof, however, comes exclusively from skills/self/spawn/lib/__tests__/spawn-gap-coverage.test.mjs's 'PROP-303c' test, which calls appendShelterCostEntry directly on a throwaway fixture file to prove the two library functions compose -- it never exercises spawn-orchestrator.mjs's real call graph, so the 'proved' status never implied production wiring existed. Sprint-2's own contract (contracts/sprint-2.md) is the sprint whose explicit job was to wire REQ-201-305's real call sites into REQ-307's orchestrator, and its 'Deferred-obligation disposition' section enumerates all 38 of sprint-1's deferred obligations across three buckets (30 targeted for closure + 3 Tier-3 + 5 additionally re-deferred) -- PROP-303c appears in NONE of the three buckets and is never mentioned anywhere in contracts/sprint-2.md, unlike its Tier-3 sibling obligations (PROP-303b/e/f), which all carry an explicit, reasoned deferral. This is a silent gap in the contract's own reconciliation, not an honest deferral. Concrete runtime consequence: skills/self/spawn/lib/treasury-gate.mjs::deriveMeasuredShelterCostUsd is fed from wake-gate.mjs's shelter-cost.jsonl read (scripts/wake-gate.mjs:149-152), which will remain permanently empty in production (nothing ever appends to it), so REQ-102's spawnThresholdUsd will forever use the static MIN_SHELTER_USD_DEFAULT (5.0) x SAFETY_MARGIN_MULTIPLIER_DEFAULT (2) = $10 floor, never the real, measured Akash lease cost REQ-102/REQ-303's own design intends to converge toward. Separately, because leaseId is never persisted to any durable record (not the active ledger row -- buildChildSpec's schema has no leaseId/dseq field -- and not any failure row), there is no way, even for a currently-active child, to look up its own Akash dseq from this feature's own state; this blocks the manual/operator-driven lease reconciliation the spec's own REQ-402 Edge Cases text (behavioral-spec.md:2927-2931) names as the intended mitigation for an abandoned/orphaned lease.

evidence.testName: grep -rn "appendShelterCostEntry" skills/self/spawn/ (excluding __tests__) returns only the module's own definition (lib/shelter-cost-ledger.js) and zero production call sites; verification/fuzz-results/full-suite-116-run.log + full-suite-121-run.log confirm PROP-303c was 'proved' via spawn-gap-coverage.test.mjs's direct library-level round-trip test, never via spawn-orchestrator.mjs's real executeSpawnAttempt.
